name: Milan
tagline: A 1949 panzerotto by the Duomo, and two Michelin stars that have defined Milanese haute cuisine for half a century.

Cracco in Galleria.description: Carlo Cracco's table inside the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, in the heart of Milan. One Michelin star and a 93/100 score in the Gambero Rosso guide.

Aimo e Nadia.description: A Milanese haute cuisine institution for more than half a century. Two Michelin stars.

Luini.description: The bakery that introduced the Puglian panzerotto to Milan, since 1949, steps from the Duomo.

Seta by Antonio Guida.description: Antonio Guida's cuisine at the Mandarin Oriental Milano, Mediterranean technique of the highest precision. Two Michelin stars.

Enrico Bartolini al MUDEC.description: Inside the Museum of Cultures, Milan's only three-Michelin-star table.

Sadler.description: Claudio Sadler's signature cuisine in the Brera district, French classical technique applied to Italian ingredients. One Michelin star.

Ristorante Berton.description: Andrea Berton's refined, ingredient-driven Italian cooking in the Porta Nuova district. One Michelin star.

Contraste.description: Uruguayan chef Matias Perdomo runs one of Milan's most creative tables, inside a period building near Porta Romana. One Michelin star.

Iyo.description: Italy's only Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant, founded by Claudio Liu near the CityLife district.

Joia.description: Pietro Leemann opened the first vegetarian restaurant in Europe to win a Michelin star, in 1996. It remains the benchmark for plant-based fine dining.

Trippa.description: Diego Rossi's trattoria in Porta Romana reinvented offal cooking and popular Milanese recipes since opening in 2015.

Erba Brusca.description: Market and kitchen-garden cooking on the banks of the Naviglio Pavese, with a terrace among aromatic herbs.

Al Pont de Ferr.description: An osteria by the iron bridge on the Naviglio Grande, honest Italian cooking recognized with the Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Ratanà.description: Cesare Battisti reinterprets Milanese and Lombard tradition inside a former tram depot facing the Bosco Verticale, since 2009.

Torre - Fondazione Prada.description: On the sixth floor of the Fondazione Prada tower designed by Rem Koolhaas, with panoramic views and Italian-rooted cooking.

Ceresio 7.description: Rooftop restaurant and pools atop the former Enel headquarters, owned by the Dsquared2 designers, with 360-degree views over Milan.

Bar Basso.description: Open since 1947, this is the birthplace of the Negroni Sbagliato, served in its iconic oversized glasses.

Camparino in Galleria.description: On the corner of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II where Gaspare Campari opened his first bar in 1867. A historic reference point for Milanese aperitivo.

Marchesi 1824.description: Milan's historic pastry shop, founded in 1824 and now part of the Prada group, celebrated for its panettone and handcrafted sweets.

Cova.description: Café and pastry shop opened in 1817 near La Scala, now owned by LVMH, located on Via Montenapoleone since 1950.

Sant Ambroeus.description: Milanese pastry shop and tearoom since 1936, in its historic home on Corso Matteotti, birthplace of panettone gelato.

Pasticceria Cucchi.description: Historic pastry shop since 1936 on the corner of Corso Genova, recognized as one of Milan's official historic shops.

Antico Ristorante Boeucc.description: Milan's oldest restaurant, founded in 1696, now on Corso Monforte; it once served Verdi, Donizetti and Toscanini.

Trattoria Masuelli San Marco.description: Family-run trattoria since 1921 on Viale Umbria, celebrated for its cotoletta alla milanese and deep wine list.

Antica Trattoria della Pesa.description: A 19th-century trattoria near Porta Volta, named after the old customs weighing station once located there; classic Milanese cooking.

Dongiò.description: Calabrian trattoria in Porta Romana since 1987, recognized with the Michelin Bib Gourmand for its value and quality.

Langosteria.description: The flagship of the Langosteria group in the Tortona district, Milan's benchmark for raw fish and seafood since 2007.

Da Giacomo.description: A Milanese seafood classic since 1958, in its historic Via Sottocorno home since 1989.

Giacomo Arengario.description: Inside the Museo del Novecento, with direct views of the Duomo; classic Italian cooking in an art deco setting.

Armani/Ristorante.description: On the seventh floor of the Armani Hotel Milano on Via Manzoni, Italian fine dining with Giorgio Armani's minimalist aesthetic.

VIVA Viviana Varese.description: Chef Viviana Varese cooks seasonal seafood and vegetables on the second floor of Eataly Smeraldo. One Michelin star.

Tokuyoshi.description: Chef Yoji Tokuyoshi, formerly Massimo Bottura's right hand, crosses Italian ingredients with Japanese technique. One Michelin star since 2016.

Pisacco.description: A bistro on Via Solferino founded by Andrea Berton, essential Italian cooking recognized with the Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Un Posto a Milano.description: Kitchen, bar and garden inside Cascina Cuccagna, an 18th-century farmhouse restored in the heart of Porta Romana.

Spontini.description: A historic pizzeria since 1953, famous for its single tall, spongy margherita slice, near the Duomo.

Princi.description: A bakery and forno open since 1986, the reference point for bread, focaccia and pizza al taglio in central Milan.

Panificio Davide Longoni.description: Davide Longoni's sourdough bakery, a pioneer of ancient-grain bread in Milan.

Nottingham Forest.description: Dario Comino's cocktail bar, the Italian pioneer of clarification and fermentation techniques in mixology.

Rita.description: One of the pioneering cocktail bars of the Navigli, open since 2002, classic cocktails in a small, always-packed space.

Mag Cafè.description: A cocktail bar with vintage decor on the banks of the Naviglio Grande, a popular aperitivo stop in the Navigli district.

La Ravioleria Sarpi.description: A stall making hand-folded dumplings to order in the heart of Milan's Chinatown, on Via Paolo Sarpi.

Gelateria Umberto 1934.description: A historic gelateria since 1934 on Piazza Cinque Giornate, artisanal gelato made with traditional recipes.

Al Matarel.description: A traditional trattoria in Brera since 1962, faithful to cassoeula and ossobuco without reinterpretation.

Osteria del Binari.description: A former railway workers' club turned into an osteria with a garden, traditional Milanese cooking near Porta Genova.

Latteria di San Marco.description: A tiny nine-table trattoria in Brera, no reservations, run by the same family for more than forty years.

El Brellin.description: A restaurant on the Vicolo dei Lavandai, the Naviglio Grande's old public washhouse, regional Lombard cooking in an 18th-century house.

Pizzium.description: The original Pizzium, opened in 2017 on Via Procaccini, contemporary Neapolitan pizza with selected Italian ingredients.

Berberè.description: A pizzeria chain born in Emilia-Romagna that brought contemporary sourdough pizza and seasonal toppings to Milan, with a branch in Isola.

Ciacco.description: An artisanal gelateria on Via Spadari near the Duomo, awarded the Tre Coni by the Gambero Rosso guide.

Trattoria Madonnina.description: A trattoria in a building documented since 1722, near Porta Ticinese, uncompromising traditional Lombard cooking.

Gino Sorbillo - Pizza Gourmand.description: The Milan outpost of Neapolitan pizzaiolo Gino Sorbillo, near the Duomo, using the same long-fermentation dough as his historic Naples shop.

Eataly Milano Smeraldo.description: A large Italian food market with restaurants, bakery and shop, housed in the former Cinema Smeraldo near Porta Garibaldi.

Mercato Centrale Milano.description: A food market inside the Stazione Centrale, with more than twenty stalls from Italian artisan producers open all day.

10 Corso Como Café.description: The café of the 10 Corso Como concept store, a meeting point for Milanese fashion and design since 1990.

Radetzky Café.description: A historic Milanese aperitivo bar on Corso Garibaldi, open all day from early morning until the small hours.

Trattoria Aurora.description: A Liberty-style trattoria in the Tortona district, celebrated for its ossobuco, cotoletta and saffron risotto.

Giannino dal 1899.description: A historic restaurant near Stazione Centrale, serving traditional Italian and Milanese cooking for more than a century.

La Brisa.description: A restaurant with an inner garden next to the remains of a Roman palace, between Piazza Cordusio and Castello Sforzesco.

Bulk Mixology Food & Bar.description: A mixology bar inside the ViU Hotel near Porta Garibaldi, signature cocktails with house-made spirits and ferments.

Il Massimo del Gelato.description: An artisanal gelateria since 2001 in the Sempione district, specializing in chocolate variations.
